title_en: Telephone Reply of the Administrative Division of the Supreme People's Court on Whether the Township People's Government Shall Be Liable for Damages Caused by Staff of the Township Public Security Office Who Intentionally Injure a Party in the Course of Performing Duties

articles.content_en:
Telephone Reply of the Administrative Adjudication Tribunal of the Supreme People's Court
on Whether the Township People's Government Shall Bear Liability for Damage Caused by the Deliberate Injury of a Party by a Staff Member of the Township Security Office in the Performance of Duties
(October 10, 1991)

Higher People's Court of Sichuan Province:

Your Request for Instructions on Whether the Township People's Government Shall Bear Compensation Liability for Damage Caused by the Deliberate Injury of a Party by a Staff Member of the Township Security Office in the Performance of Duties (Chuan Fa Yan [1991] No. 45) has been received. Upon study, we agree with your second opinion.

Appendix:

Request for Instructions of the Higher People's Court of Sichuan Province
on Whether the Township People's Government Shall Bear Compensation Liability for Damage Caused by the Deliberate Injury of a Party by a Staff Member of the Township Security Office in the Performance of Duties
September 20, 1991 Chuan Fa Yan [1991] No. 45

Supreme People's Court:

In some localities of our province, cases have occurred from time to time where staff members of township security offices deliberately injure parties in the performance of public security management duties, with some victims disabled as a result. With respect to whether the township people's government shall bear compensation liability for such damage, the relevant departments and internal courts hold divergent understandings. In our discussions, three opinions have been put forward:

First opinion: The township security office, under the leadership of the township government and the guidance of the public security substation, is responsible for managing the public security within its jurisdiction. Where its staff members, in the performance of public security management duties, violate laws and discipline by injuring a party, the damage is not caused by the proper performance of duties; the actor shall bear compensation liability, and the township government shall not bear compensation liability.

Second opinion: Article 68 of the Administrative Procedure Law provides: "Where a specific administrative act taken by an administrative organ or its staff infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen, legal person, or other organization and causes damage, the administrative organ shall be liable for compensation." Pursuant to this provision, the township government shall bear compensation liability for losses caused by the tortious acts of the staff members of the security office. After paying compensation, the township government may, depending on the circumstances, order the actor to bear part or all of the compensation expenses.

Third opinion: Where a staff member of the security office, in the performance of public security management duties, violates laws and discipline by injuring a party, the damage is not caused by a specific administrative act but constitutes a civil tort committed in the performance of duties. Article 121 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Where a state organ or its staff, in the performance of duties, infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen or legal person and causes damage, it shall bear civil liability." Pursuant to this provision, the township government shall bear civil compensation liability.

We tend to favor the second opinion. Whether this is correct, please instruct.
